{{short description|Tunisian-American mathematician}}
'''Mohammed Salah Baouendi''' ({{langx|ar|محمد صالح باوندي}}; October 12, 1937 in [[Tunis]] – December 24, 2011 in [[La Jolla, California]]) was a [[Tunisian people|Tunisian]]-American [[mathematician]] who worked as a Distinguished Professor of Mathematics at the [[University of California, San Diego]]. His research concerned [[partial differential equation]]s and the theory of [[several complex variables]].<ref name="ucsd">{{citation|url=http://physicalsciences.ucsd.edu/news/2012/salahbaouendi.html|title=M. Salah Baouendi (1937-2011)|website=News from the Physical Sciences|publisher=[[University of California, San Diego]]|year=2012|accessdate=2015-01-09|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150110084143/http://physicalsciences.ucsd.edu/news/2012/salahbaouendi.html|archivedate=2015-01-10}}.</ref><ref name="imu">{{citation|url=http://www.mathunion.org/imu-net/archive/2011/imu-net-051/|title=Passing away of professor Salah Baouendi|first=László|last=Lovász|authorlink=László Lovász|journal=IMU-Net|volume=51|date=January 2012|publisher=[[International Mathematical Union]]|accessdate=2015-01-09}}.</ref>

==Education and career==
Baouendi moved from Tunis to France after finishing his [[Baccalauréat]] in the high school [[Sadiki College]], and earned a [[Licentiate (degree)|licence]] (a French undergraduate degree) in 1961 from the [[University of Paris|Sorbonne]].<ref name="imu"/> In this he had the assistance of a scholarship from the Tunisian government, which however demanded that he return to Tunis afterwards to become a schoolteacher. After the intervention of [[Laurent Schwartz]], Baouendi was allowed to return to France for his graduate studies.<ref name="mgc">{{citation|title=A Mathematician Grappling With His Century|first=Laurent|last=Schwartz|authorlink=Laurent Schwartz|publisher=Birkhäuser|year=2001|isbn=9783764360528|page=268|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xVrC7ek7iRwC&pg=PA268}}.</ref> He completed a doctorate in 1967 from the [[University of Paris-Sud]] (then part of the [[University of Paris]]), under the supervision of [[Bernard Malgrange]], with a dissertation concerning [[elliptic operator]]s.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=16459}}</ref> Schwartz attempted to secure for him a suitable academic position in Tunis, in which he would be allowed to conduct research and collaborate with mathematicians from other countries,<ref name="mgc"/> and Baouendi became an associate professor at [[Tunis University]] in 1968, but his administrative struggles there were too much, and he left in 1970. After a short stay at the [[University of Nice Sophia Antipolis|University of Nice]], Baouendi moved in 1971 to the USA.<ref name="imu"/><ref name="mgc"/>

Baouendi's first American faculty position was at [[Purdue University]]. During his tenure at Purdue, he was promoted to full professor in 1973, became department chair from 1980 to 1987, and also held visiting positions at [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]], the [[University of Chicago]], and [[Rutgers University]]. He became a Distinguished Professor at UCSD in 1988 (giving up his Purdue professorship in 1990).<ref name="cv">[http://www.math.ucsd.edu/~sbaouend/cv.pdf Curriculum vitae], accessed 2015-01-09.</ref> He was a co-founder of two journals, ''Communications in Partial Differential Equations'' and ''Mathematical Research Letters''.<ref name="ucsd"/>

==Awards and honors==
Baouendi was given the Prix d'Aumale of the French Academy of Sciences in 1969. He was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 1974. He and his wife, mathematician [[Linda Preiss Rothschild]], were jointly awarded the [[Stefan Bergman#The Bergman Prize|Stefan Bergman Prize]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in 2003.<ref name="cv"/><ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200304/people.pdf|title=Baouendi and Rothschild Receive 2003 Bergman Prize|department=Mathematics People|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|pages=480–481|volume=50|issue=4|date=April 2003}}.</ref> In 2005 he became a [[fellow]] of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref name="ucsd"/><ref name="cv"/>
